sections.heading: Planning your Hudson Place Residences interior
sections.text:
District 5 sits between a business-park working life and older west-coast housing, so many owners here need a home that can take weekday work without turning the living room into a permanent office. The usual answer is built-in: a desk and storage wall in a common bedroom or a defined alcove, a living-room joinery wall that hides screens and cables, full-height wardrobes, and a kitchen of fitted cabinets with a tall pantry. Maison will design those pieces to your approved plan, as custom carpentry rather than loose, flat-pack furniture. We can show a full room or a closer study of a desk wall, a wardrobe interior or a kitchen counter, depending on what you need to decide.

No official floor plan is on file, so this page does not list typologies or room sizes. Blossoms by the Park, listed at Slim Barracks Rise in the same district, is a nearby page on this site; it is not a typologies reference for Hudson Place. We will also not invent walking times to one-north, to a motorway, or to any MRT station. Check your own stack, facing and the management handbook before you commit to blinds, a bench or a balcony screen.

When a key date is confirmed, work backwards: leave time for defects and rectification, a measured survey, renovation approval, and fabrication. A moderate carpentry scope is often planned at about six to ten weeks on site after approvals, as an editorial planning figure only. WhatsApp Maison with your unit type and approved plan when you have them. We are an independent designer and are not affiliated with the developer.
